she is one in whom the delusion caused by the *guṇas* has ceased and become stilled.

The sequence of composition: He describes her liberation while living (jīvanmukti) with three and a half verses. And then, because she was one whose "state of being a living soul" (jīvabhāva)—that is, the condition of having attained a living state—had ceased; because of that reality, she, being free from afflictions and having attained bliss, did not remember her body as being the true self.
The logical connection follows from what precedes. ||27||

Viśvanātha: Furthermore, he states that the secondary fruit of devotion—which has been described as "that which quickly wears away the storehouse"—has arisen therein: "Because of the state of having ceased the affliction of the individual soul" (*jīvasya āpattiḥ*);

that is, because of the reality (*tattvam*) of that [devotion] in which the ignorance consisting of calamity has ceased for the individual self (*jīvātman*), [the devotee] is one whose afflictions (*kleśa*) have been exhausted.

For this very reason, there is the attainment of liberation (*nirvṛti*) by the trustworthy one (*āpta*). Alternatively, because he is the mother of the Blessed One, that which is inherently free from ignorance is also described in that way, just as it is said: "This Self is free from evil" (*apahatapāpmā*). According to the view of the devotees, [the Lord] is peaceful, having turned away from the delusion of the bliss of meditation; [he is free from] the wandering or delusion regarding qualities and sense objects.
She whose [nature] is wandering; "self" refers to the body. ||27||
His body, though nourished by others and not emaciated due to the presence of wealth,
shone as if covered with soot, like a fire enveloped in smoke.

Śrīdhara: He whose nourishment and sustenance were provided by the Vidyādharīs created from the mud by others who were themselves superior; he was not emaciated because mental anguish (ādhi) was impossible for him;
and though covered with impurities, he shone.

The sequential composition: Not only this much, but his body also became non-emaciated (*akṛśa*). Of what kind? To that he says: "from the other" (*parataḥ*). This is the reason for its non-emaciation. "Due to the impossibility of [worldly] possessions" (*ādhyasambhavāt*); the sense is: due to the bliss of the Lord's descent (*āveśa*). For this very reason, how did it shine? To that he says: "by impurities" (*malaiḥ*).
Thus [it is said]. The word "also" (api) is to be supplied. In this regard, the illustration is: "accompanied by smoke. ||28||
Viśvanātha: He describes her condition at that time:

her body was nourished—that is, sustained—by others, namely the *vidyādharī* women created from the mud; and she was not emaciated by mental anguish (*ādhi*) because of the bliss of being possessed by the Lord, which rendered such suffering impossible—she was full of contentment (*nirvṛti*).
"Because it is stated in the medical treatises that [the dosage] must be made very large. ||28||
With his intellect entered by Vāsudeva, he did not perceive his own body— composed of ascetic power and yoga, with disheveled hair and no clothes— to be protected by fate.
Śrīdhara: "Protected by destiny" means sustained by the karma that has been commenced. ||29||

The sequential arrangement: [He protects those who have approached Him] according to the principle stated in Bhāgavata Purāṇa 2.2.6: "Why would the Unconquered One not protect those protected by the divine Śrī Vāsudeva himself? ||29||
Viśvanātha: Protected by fate, that is, guarded by the Blessed One. ||29||
Thus, by the path taught by Kapila,
she soon attained the Blessed One, the Supreme Self, who is the extinction of Brahma.
Śrīdhara: Nirvāṇa is said to be eternal. ||30||

The sequential composition [of the work] is as follows: by means of a particular manifestation of light, he attained the Blessed Lord, the Master of Mahāvaikuṇṭha, who is known as both the Supreme Self (paramātman) and Brahman; and he attained that state of Nirvāṇa in such a way that it was preceded by the cessation of the sufferings of saṃsāra—this is the meaning.
Because even its appearance does not persist at that time. ||30||

Viśvanātha: [He refers to] the Supreme, the most excellent Self, the Blessed Lord, who has become the Master through dispassion (*vairāgya*). Now, did she not attain *nirvāṇa*? To this he says: "The Blessed Lord himself is her *brahman*-liberation"—thus he says "Brahman. Or rather, as in the passage beginning with "the attainment of Adhokṣaja here," that...

Based on the statement in the seventh book, "The wise know the bliss of Brahman-nirvāṇa" (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.7.37), he brought his own son Kapila—who was designated by the term "Brahman-nirvāṇa"—to achieve dispassion for the sake of Kapila [the sage]. ||30||
That most holy field, renowned throughout the three worlds,
was known by the name Siddhapada, where she attained perfect accomplishment.
Śrīdhara: O hero Vidura! "Upeyuṣī" means she has arrived. ||31||
Kramasaṃdarbha: Not commented upon.
Viśvanātha: O hero Vidura! ||31||
O gentle one, that mortal body of hers, shaken off by yoga, became a river—
the foremost of streams, bestowing success and frequented by the perfected ones.
Śrīdhara: O gentle one, her mortal body became a river.
Of what nature was it? It was one in which the impurities of the bodily elements (mārtyā daihikā dhātumalāḥ) had been shaken off and dissolved through yoga.
The sequence of events is as follows: although she remained in Mahāvaikuṇṭha in another form, just like Śrī Kapiladeva.
It is well known in the world that she wanders everywhere with her own body for the sake of liberating the world;
having assumed the form of a river and become its presiding deity herself, she remains pervading even the earth—thus he says: "Of her" (tasyāḥ). ||32||
Viśvanātha: O gentle one, her mortal body became a river. Of what nature was it?
It was that from which the impurities of the mortal elements had been shaken off and dissolved through yoga. (32)
The venerable Kapila, the great yogi, having taken leave of his mother from his father’s hermitage, departed toward the north-eastern direction.
Śrīdhara: It was stated that Kapila also departed; he elaborates on that very point with three verses beginning with "Kapilo 'pi. "Samanujñāpya" means having requested permission. ||33||
The sequence of composition: first, he initially proceeded toward the northern direction alone from the practice of virtuous conduct;
afterwards, he attained stability only at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean—this is the meaning. ||33||

Viśvanātha: It was stated that Kapila departed; he elaborates on that very point in three verses beginning with "Kapilo 'pi. Having requested permission—that is, having sought leave—first, in accordance with the conduct of the virtuous, he went toward the northern direction alone. The meaning is that afterwards, he attained a state of stability at the very confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean.
Being praised by Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, sages, and hosts of Apsarases,
he was offered a worthy dwelling by the Ocean.
Śrīdhara: To whom [the Lord] gave the offering of honor, the water for the feet, and a dwelling. ||34||
The sequential arrangement: the pair beginning with "siddhā" [is explained]. ||34||
Viśvanātha: This has not been explained.
He remains established in yoga, praised by the teachers of Sāṅkhya, fully concentrated for the sake of the peace of all the three worlds.
Śrīdhara: He remains composed, worthy of tranquility. ||35||

The sequence of composition [is as follows], Viśvanātha: [this] has not been explained. O sinless one, my dear, that which I was asked by you has now been related—this purifying dialogue between Kapila and Devahūtī.
Śrīdhara concludes the meaning of the section with the words "This" (etad): [it means] "by you," that is, by thee. ||36||
The sequence of composition: regarding the word "etad" (this) here, Puṇyāraṇya says it means "evam" (thus). ||36||
Viśvanātha: This has not been explained.
He who listens to this, he who recites it—the teaching of the sage Kapila, the secret of self-yoga—[attains the goal].
One whose intellect is fixed upon the Blessed One, the one whose banner is Garuda, attains the lotus feet of the Blessed One.
Śrīdhara: He states the fruit of hearing and chanting this [name] with the words "He who... [etc.]. "Suvarṇaketau" means on him whose banner is Garuḍa. "Upalabhate" means he attains. ||37||
The sequential composition: demonstrating through the fruit the intended meaning spoken by Śrī Kapiladeva, he confirms that very state of Śrī Devahūti with the words "He who this...
He who merely explains it, or he who merely hears it—what more need be said of him who practices it, or even more so?
The meaning is "just like the illustrious Devahūti. ||37||

Viśvanātha: Demonstrating through the result the intended meaning spoken by the illustrious Kapiladeva, he further confirms such a destiny for Devahūtī with the words "He who this... and so on. He who explains it even briefly, or he who hears it even briefly—what need is there to mention one who practices it? And what need is there to mention Śrī Devahūtī, who has practiced it even more? Upa...

"He attains the state of an attendant with exceeding love for the purpose of serving the lotus feet of the Lord"— thus it is said in the *Harṣiṇī*, which reveals the essential meaning for the hearts of devotees.
This concludes the thirty-third chapter of the third book, appropriately joined to the assembly of the virtuous.
I, who am ignorant of the scriptures, do not understand the meaning of this glorious Bhagavad-gītā;
nevertheless, I compose this commentary out of a desire for my own intellect to attain union with it.
Bowing down and seeking forgiveness for his own offense, this person implores favor from the entire universe, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass.
This commentary on the Third Skandha was completed on the eighth lunar day at the foot of the Kalpa-tree of Śrī Vṛndāvana, on the banks of the Yamunā.

Thus ends the narrative of Kapila, titled "The Story of Kapila," within the dialogue between Vidura and Maitreya, in the Third Canto of the Vaiyāsikī Saṃhitā, the *Pāramahaṃsya* compendium of the *Brahmasūtra-bhāṣya* in the glorious *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*, the Great Purāṇa.
The Thirty-third Chapter.
